content.text: An enum (short for enumeration) is a special Java data type used to define a fixed set of named constants.

subsections.heading: 🔹 Why Use enum Instead of final Constants?

items: Enums are type-safe and group related constants together.
All enum constants are public static final implicitly.
Enums are reference types, similar to classes and interfaces.
Enums extend java.lang.Enum implicitly (cannot extend other classes).
Enum constructors are invoked automatically and cannot be called using new.

content.text: You can define additional information for each constant:

content.code:
Day: SUNDAY Value: 1
Day: MONDAY Value: 2
Day: TUESDAY Value: 3
Day: WEDNESDAY Value: 4
Day: THURSDAY Value: 5
Day: FRIDAY Value: 6
Day: SATURDAY Value: 7

items: Enums are preferred for defining constants with meaningful names and values.
Provide type safety and organized structure.
Can include constructors and methods for additional behavior.
Used in many real-world applications like status codes, user roles, days, etc.
